verses.en: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
verses.zh: 在耶路撒冷作王、大卫的儿子、传道者的言语。

words.g: in + Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine

verses.en: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
verses.zh: 传道者说：虚空的虚空，虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。

verses.en: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
verses.zh: 人一切的劳碌，就是他在日光之下的劳碌，有甚么益处呢？

verses.en: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
verses.zh: 一代过去，一代又来，地却永远长存。

verses.en: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
verses.zh: 日头出来，日头落下，急归所出之地。

verses.en: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
verses.zh: 风往南刮，又向北转，不住地旋转，而且返回转行原道。

verses.en: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
verses.zh: 江河都往海里流，海却不满；江河从何处流，仍归还何处。

words.g: the + a stream, especially a winter torrent
which, that + the + a stream, especially a winter torrent

verses.en: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.zh: 万事令人厌烦（或译：万物满有困乏），人不能说尽。眼看，看不饱；耳听，听不足。

verses.en: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.
verses.zh: 已有的事后必再有；已行的事后必再行。日光之下并无新事。

verses.en: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
verses.zh: 岂有一件事人能指着说这是新的？哪知，在我们以前的世代早已有了。

words.g: extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
verses.zh: 已过的世代，无人记念；将来的世代，后来的人也不记念。

verses.en: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.zh: 我传道者在耶路撒冷作过以色列的王。

words.g: in + Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine

verses.en: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
verses.zh: 我专心用智慧寻求、查究天下所做的一切事，乃知神叫世人所经练的是极重的劳苦。

words.g: and + to + to meander  about, especially fortrade or reconnoitring
ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 我见日光之下所做的一切事，都是虚空，都是捕风。

words.g: and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
verses.zh: 弯曲的，不能变直；缺少的，不能足数。

verses.en: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
verses.zh: 我心里议论说：我得了大智慧，胜过我以前在耶路撒冷的众人，而且我心中多经历智慧和知识的事。

words.g: Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine

verses.en: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 我又专心察明智慧、狂妄，和愚昧，乃知这也是捕风。

verses.en: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
verses.zh: 因为多有智慧，就多有愁烦；加增知识的，就加增忧伤。

verses.en: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.
verses.zh: 我心里说：「来吧，我以喜乐试试你，你好享福！」谁知，这也是虚空。

verses.en: I said of laughter, “It is foolishness;” and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”
verses.zh: 我指嬉笑说：「这是狂妄。」论喜乐说：「有何功效呢？」

verses.en: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their lives.
verses.zh: 我心里察究，如何用酒使我肉体舒畅，我心却仍以智慧引导我；又如何持住愚昧，等我看明世人，在天下一生当行何事为美。

words.g: to meander  about, especially fortrade or reconnoitring
to + to draw, used in a great variety of applications

verses.en: I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.
verses.zh: 我为自己动大工程，建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，

verses.en: I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit.
verses.zh: 修造园囿，在其中栽种各样果木树；

words.g: and + to strike in, i.e. fix

verses.en: I made myself pools of water, to water the forest where trees were grown.
verses.zh: 挖造水池，用以浇灌嫩小的树木。

words.g: to + to quaff, i.e.  to irrigate or furnish apotion to

verses.en: I bought male servants and female servants, and had servants born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all who were before me in Jerusalem.
verses.zh: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的仆婢；又有许多牛群羊群，胜过以前在耶路撒冷众人所有的。

words.g: in + Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine

verses.en: I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men: musical instruments of all sorts.
verses.zh: 我又为自己积蓄金银和君王的财宝，并各省的财宝；又得唱歌的男女和世人所喜爱的物，并许多的妃嫔。

words.g: and + the + a judgeship, i.e. jurisdiction

verses.en: So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.
verses.zh: 这样，我就日见昌盛，胜过以前在耶路撒冷的众人。我的智慧仍然存留。

words.g: in + Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine

verses.en: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
verses.zh: 凡我眼所求的，我没有留下不给它的；我心所乐的，我没有禁止不享受的；因我的心为我一切所劳碌的快乐，这就是我从劳碌中所得的分。

words.g: to debar  from benefit or injury

verses.en: Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
verses.zh: 后来，我察看我手所经营的一切事和我劳碌所成的功。谁知都是虚空，都是捕风；在日光之下毫无益处。

words.g: and + in + toil, i.e. wearing effort
and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly; for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which has been done long ago.
verses.zh: 我转念观看智慧、狂妄，和愚昧。在王以后而来的人还能做甚么呢？也不过行早先所行的就是了。

words.g: which, that + to come, go in
extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
verses.zh: 我便看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗。

verses.en: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness—and yet I perceived that one event happens to them all.
verses.zh: 智慧人的眼目光明（光明：原文是在他头上），愚昧人在黑暗里行。我却看明有一件事，这两等人都必遇见。

words.g: and + the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly
which, that + something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune

verses.en: Then I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
verses.zh: 我就心里说：「愚昧人所遇见的，我也必遇见，我为何更有智慧呢？」我心里说，这也是虚空。

words.g: like + something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune
the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no memory forever, since in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the wise man must die just like the fool!
verses.zh: 智慧人和愚昧人一样，永远无人记念，因为日后都被忘记；可叹智慧人死亡，与愚昧人无异。

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly
in + which, that + extent of time, i.e. a great while
to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of
the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 我所以恨恶生命；因为在日光之下所行的事我都以为烦恼，都是虚空，都是捕风。

words.g: and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
verses.zh: 我恨恶一切的劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌，因为我得来的必留给我以后的人。

verses.en: Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all of my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
verses.zh: 那人是智慧是愚昧，谁能知道？他竟要管理我劳碌所得的，就是我在日光之下用智慧所得的。这也是虚空。

words.g: and + which, that + to be wise

verses.en: Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.
verses.zh: 故此，我转想我在日光之下所劳碌的一切工作，心便绝望。

words.g: to + to desist, i.e.  to despond

verses.en: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with skillfulness; yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.zh: 因为有人用智慧、知识、灵巧所劳碌得来的，却要留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，也是大患。

words.g: which, that + toil, i.e. wearing effort + +him/his/it

verses.en: For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?
verses.zh: 人在日光之下劳碌累心，在他一切的劳碌上得着甚么呢？

verses.en: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail is grief; yes, even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
verses.zh: 因为他日日忧虑，他的劳苦成为愁烦，连夜间心也不安。这也是虚空。

words.g: ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair + +him/his/it

verses.en: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.zh: 人莫强如吃喝，且在劳碌中享福，我看这也是出于神的手。

verses.en: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
verses.zh: 论到吃用、享福，谁能胜过我呢？

verses.en: For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 神喜悦谁，就给谁智慧、知识，和喜乐；惟有罪人，神使他劳苦，叫他将所收聚的、所堆积的归给神所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

words.g: ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair
to + to gather for any purpose
and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
verses.zh: 凡事都有定期，天下万务都有定时。

verses.en: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
verses.zh: 生有时，死有时；栽种有时，拔出所栽种的也有时；

words.g: to + to strike in, i.e. fix

verses.en: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.zh: 杀戮有时，医治有时；拆毁有时，建造有时；

words.g: to + to smite with deadly intent
to + to mend , i.e.  to cure

verses.en: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.zh: 哭有时，笑有时；哀恸有时，跳舞有时；

words.g: to tear the hair and beat the breasts
to stamp, i.e. to spring about

verses.en: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.zh: 抛掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时；怀抱有时，不怀抱有时；

words.g: to + to widen , i.e.  recede or  remove

verses.en: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.zh: 寻找有时，失落有时；保守有时，舍弃有时；

verses.en: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.zh: 撕裂有时，缝补有时；静默有时，言语有时；

words.g: to + to rend, literally or figuratively
to + to hush or keep quiet

verses.en: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
verses.zh: 喜爱有时，恨恶有时；争战有时，和好有时。

verses.en: What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?
verses.zh: 这样看来，做事的人在他的劳碌上有甚么益处呢？

verses.en: I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
verses.zh: 我见神叫世人劳苦，使他们在其中受经练。

words.g: the + ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
verses.zh: 神造万物，各按其时成为美好，又将永生（原文是永远）安置在世人心里。然而神从始至终的作为，人不能参透。

words.g: from + failure, i.e. nothing or destruction

verses.en: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
verses.zh: 我知道世人，莫强如终身喜乐行善；

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
verses.zh: 并且人人吃喝，在他一切劳碌中享福，这也是神的恩赐。

verses.en: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
verses.zh: 我知道神一切所做的都必永存；无所增添，无所减少。神这样行，是要人在他面前存敬畏的心。

verses.en: That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago. God seeks again that which is passed away.
verses.zh: 现今的事早先就有了，将来的事早已也有了，并且神使已过的事重新再来（或译：并且神再寻回已过的事）。

words.g: extent of time, i.e. a great while
extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: Moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
verses.zh: 我又见日光之下，在审判之处有奸恶，在公义之处也有奸恶。

verses.en: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
verses.zh: 我心里说，神必审判义人和恶人；因为在那里，各样事务，一切工作，都有定时。

verses.en: I said in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals.
verses.zh: 我心里说，这乃为世人的缘故，是神要试验他们，使他们觉得自己不过像兽一样。

verses.en: For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals, for all is vanity.
verses.zh: 因为世人遭遇的，兽也遭遇，所遭遇的都是一样：这个怎样死，那个也怎样死，气息都是一样。人不能强于兽，都是虚空。

words.g: something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune
and + something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune
and + something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune

verses.en: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
verses.zh: 都归一处，都是出于尘土，也都归于尘土。

verses.en: Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
verses.zh: 谁知道人的灵是往上升，兽的魂是下入地呢？

words.g: to + the upper part, used only adverbially with prefix upward

verses.en: Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who can bring him to see what will be after him?
verses.zh: 故此，我见人莫强如在他经营的事上喜乐，因为这是他的分。他身后的事谁能使他回来得见呢？

verses.en: Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
verses.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下所行的一切欺压。看哪，受欺压的流泪，且无人安慰；欺压他们的有势力，也无人安慰他们。

words.g: the + used in plural masculine as abstractly, tyranny
the + used in plural masculine as abstractly, tyranny

verses.en: Therefore I praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive.
verses.zh: 因此，我赞叹那早已死的死人，胜过那还活着的活人。

words.g: and + to address in aloud tone, i.e.  loud
which, that + extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.zh: 并且我以为那未曾生的，就是未见过日光之下恶事的，比这两等人更强。

verses.en: Then I saw all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.zh: 我又见人为一切的劳碌和各样灵巧的工作就被邻舍嫉妒。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

words.g: and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.
verses.zh: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 满了一把，得享安静，强如满了两把，劳碌捕风。

words.g: and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.
verses.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下有一件虚空的事：

verses.en: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
verses.zh: 有人孤单无二，无子无兄，竟劳碌不息，眼目也不以钱财为足。他说：「我劳劳碌碌，刻苦自己，不享福乐，到底是为谁呢？」这也是虚空，是极重的劳苦。

words.g: and + ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
verses.zh: 两个人总比一个人好，因为二人劳碌同得美好的果效。

verses.en: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
verses.zh: 若是跌倒，这人可以扶起他的同伴；若是孤身跌倒，没有别人扶起他来，这人就有祸了。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
verses.zh: 再者，二人同睡就都暖和，一人独睡怎能暖和呢？

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.zh: 有人攻胜孤身一人，若有二人便能敌挡他；三股合成的绳子不容易折断。

words.g: and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn’t know how to receive admonition any more.
verses.zh: 贫穷而有智慧的少年人胜过年老不肯纳谏的愚昧王。

words.g: something born, i.e. a lad or offspring
and + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
verses.zh: 这人是从监牢中出来作王，在他国中，生来原是贫穷的。

verses.en: I saw all the living who walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.
verses.zh: 我见日光之下一切行动的活人都随从那第二位，就是起来代替老王的少年人。

words.g: the + something born, i.e. a lad or offspring

verses.en: There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was—yet those who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 他所治理的众人就是他的百姓，多得无数；在他后来的人尚且不喜悦他。这真是虚空，也是捕风。

verses.en: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
verses.zh: 你到神的殿要谨慎脚步；因为近前听，胜过愚昧人献祭（或译：胜过献愚昧人的祭），他们本不知道所做的是恶。

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
verses.zh: 你在神面前不可冒失开口，也不可心急发言；因为神在天上，你在地下，所以你的言语要寡少。

words.g: to tremble inwardly , i.e.  be   alarmed or agitated
the mouth , whether literal or figurative + +you/your
to be liquid or flow easily, i.e
and + thou and thee, or  ye and you

verses.en: For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words.
verses.zh: 事务多，就令人做梦；言语多，就显出愚昧。

words.g: ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
verses.zh: 你向神许愿，偿还不可迟延，因他不喜悦愚昧人，所以你许的愿应当偿还。

words.g: in + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
verses.zh: 你许愿不还，不如不许。

verses.en: Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.zh: 不可任你的口使肉体犯罪，也不可在祭司（原文是使者）面前说是错许了。为何使神因你的声音发怒，败坏你手所做的呢？

words.g: the mouth , whether literal or figurative + +you/your
to crack off, i.e.  burst out in rage
and + to wind tightly , i.e. to bind

verses.en: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words; but you must fear God.
verses.zh: 多梦和多言，其中多有虚幻，你只要敬畏神。

verses.en: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter, for one official is eyed by a higher one, and there are officials over them.
verses.zh: 你若在一省之中见穷人受欺压，并夺去公义公平的事，不要因此诧异；因有一位高过居高位的鉴察，在他们以上还有更高的。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
verses.zh: 况且地的益处归众人，就是君王也受田地的供应。

verses.en: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
verses.zh: 贪爱银子的，不因得银子知足；贪爱丰富的，也不因得利益知足。这也是虚空。

verses.en: When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
verses.zh: 货物增添，吃的人也增添，物主得甚么益处呢？不过眼看而已！

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
verses.zh: 劳碌的人不拘吃多吃少，睡得香甜；富足人的丰满却不容他睡觉。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
to + rich, whether literal or figurative

verses.en: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
verses.zh: 我见日光之下有一宗大祸患，就是财主积存资财，反害自己。

verses.en: Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
verses.zh: 因遭遇祸患，这些资财就消灭；那人若生了儿子，手里也一无所有。

words.g: in + ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.zh: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必照样赤身而去；他所劳碌得来的，手中分毫不能带去。

words.g: like + which, that + to come, go in

verses.en: This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
verses.zh: 他来的情形怎样，他去的情形也怎样。这也是一宗大祸患。他为风劳碌有甚么益处呢？

words.g: which, that + to come, go in

verses.en: All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
verses.zh: 并且他终身在黑暗中吃喝，多有烦恼，又有病患呕气。

verses.en: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
verses.zh: 我所见为善为美的，就是人在神赐他一生的日子吃喝，享受日光之下劳碌得来的好处，因为这是他的分。

verses.en: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
verses.zh: 神赐人资财丰富，使他能以吃用，能取自己的分，在他劳碌中喜乐，这乃是神的恩赐。

verses.en: For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life, because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
verses.zh: 他不多思念自己一生的年日，因为神应他的心使他喜乐。

verses.en: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:
verses.zh: 我见日光之下有一宗祸患重压在人身上，

verses.en: a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.zh: 就是人蒙神赐他资财、丰富、尊荣，以致他心里所愿的一样都不缺，只是神使他不能吃用，反有外人来吃用。这是虚空，也是祸患。

words.g: and + weight, but only figuratively in a good sense
strange, in a variety of degrees and applications

verses.en: If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he;
verses.zh: 人若生一百个儿子，活许多岁数，以致他的年日甚多，心里却不得满享福乐，又不得埋葬；据我说，那不到期而落的胎比他倒好。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
to live, whether literally or figuratively
the + something fallen, i.e. an abortion

verses.en: for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
verses.zh: 因为虚虚而来，暗暗而去，名字被黑暗遮蔽，

verses.en: Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other.
verses.zh: 并且没有见过天日，也毫无知觉；这胎，比那人倒享安息。

verses.en: Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place?
verses.zh: 那人虽然活千年，再活千年，却不享福，众人岂不都归一个地方去吗？

words.g: to live, whether literally or figuratively

verses.en: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.zh: 人的劳碌都为口腹，心里却不知足。

words.g: to + the mouth , whether literal or figurative + +him/his/it

verses.en: For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?
verses.zh: 这样看来，智慧人比愚昧人有甚么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道如何行，有甚么长处呢？

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly
to + depressed, in mind or circumstances

verses.en: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
verses.zh: 眼睛所看的比心里妄想的倒好。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

words.g: and + a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after

verses.en: Whatever has been, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is mightier than he.
verses.zh: 先前所有的，早已起了名，并知道何为人，他也不能与那比自己力大的相争。

words.g: extent of time, i.e. a great while
to + a straight course, i.e. sail direct

verses.en: For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
verses.zh: 加增虚浮的事既多，这与人有甚么益处呢？

verses.en: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?
verses.zh: 人一生虚度的日子，就如影儿经过，谁知道甚么与他有益呢？谁能告诉他身后在日光之下有甚么事呢？

verses.en: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
verses.zh: 名誉强如美好的膏油；人死的日子胜过人生的日子。

verses.en: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
verses.zh: 往遭丧的家去，强如往宴乐的家去；因为死是众人的结局，活人也必将这事放在心上。

verses.en: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
verses.zh: 忧愁强如喜笑；因为面带愁容，终必使心喜乐。

verses.en: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.zh: 智慧人的心在遭丧之家；愚昧人的心在快乐之家。

verses.en: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.zh: 听智慧人的责备，强如听愚昧人的歌唱。

verses.en: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
verses.zh: 愚昧人的笑声，好像锅下烧荆棘的爆声；这也是虚空。

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
verses.zh: 勒索使智慧人变为愚妄；贿赂能败坏人的慧心。

verses.en: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.zh: 事情的终局强如事情的起头；存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。

verses.en: Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
verses.zh: 你不要心里急躁恼怒，因为恼怒存在愚昧人的怀中。

words.g: to tremble inwardly , i.e.  be   alarmed or agitated

verses.en: Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
verses.zh: 不要说：先前的日子强过如今的日子，是甚么缘故呢？你这样问，不是出于智慧。

verses.en: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
verses.zh: 智慧和产业并好，而且见天日的人得智慧更为有益。

verses.en: For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
verses.zh: 因为智慧护庇人，好像银钱护庇人一样。惟独智慧能保全智慧人的生命。这就是知识的益处。

words.g: to live, whether literally or figuratively

verses.en: Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight which he has made crooked?
verses.zh: 你要察看神的作为；因神使为曲的，谁能变为直呢？

verses.en: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
verses.zh: 遇亨通的日子你当喜乐；遭患难的日子你当思想；因为神使这两样并列，为的是叫人查不出身后有甚么事。

verses.en: All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
verses.zh: 有义人行义，反致灭亡；有恶人行恶，倒享长寿。这都是我在虚度之日中所见过的。

verses.en: Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
verses.zh: 不要行义过分，也不要过于自逞智慧，何必自取败亡呢？

words.g: to stun , i.e. devastate or  stupefy

verses.en: Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
verses.zh: 不要行恶过分，也不要为人愚昧，何必不到期而死呢？

verses.en: It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also don’t withdraw your hand from that; for he who fears God will come out of them all.
verses.zh: 你持守这个为美，那个也不要松手；因为敬畏神的人，必从这两样出来。

verses.en: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.zh: 智慧使有智慧的人比城中十个官长更有能力。

verses.en: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn’t sin.
verses.zh: 时常行善而不犯罪的义人，世上实在没有。

verses.en: Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
verses.zh: 人所说的一切话，你不要放在心上，恐怕听见你的仆人咒诅你。

verses.en: for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
verses.zh: 因为你心里知道，自己也曾屡次咒诅别人。

words.g: thou and thee, or  ye and you

verses.en: All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise;” but it was far from me.
verses.zh: 我曾用智慧试验这一切事；我说，要得智慧，智慧却离我远。

verses.en: That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
verses.zh: 万事之理，离我甚远，而且最深，谁能测透呢？

verses.en: I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
verses.zh: 我转念，一心要知道，要考察，要寻求智慧和万事的理由；又要知道邪恶为愚昧，愚昧为狂妄。

words.g: and + to + to meander  about, especially fortrade or reconnoitring
fatness, i.e. by implication  the loin  or  the viscera

verses.en: I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
verses.zh: 我得知有等妇人比死还苦：她的心是网罗，手是锁链。凡蒙神喜悦的人必能躲避她；有罪的人却被她缠住了。

words.g: to be smooth, i.e.  to escape

verses.en: “Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find an explanation
verses.zh: 传道者说：「看哪，一千男子中，我找到一个正直人，但众女子中，没有找到一个。」我将这事一一比较，要寻求其理，我心仍要寻找，却未曾找到。

verses.en: which my soul still seeks, but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all those.
verses.zh: a

verses.en: Behold, I have only found this: that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions.”
verses.zh: 我所找到的只有一件，就是神造人原是正直，但他们寻出许多巧计。

words.g: a contrivance, i.e. actual  or mental

verses.en: Who is like the wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
verses.zh: 谁如智慧人呢？谁知道事情的解释呢？人的智慧使他的脸发光，并使他脸上的暴气改变。

verses.en: I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
verses.zh: 我劝你遵守王的命令；既指神起誓，理当如此。

words.g: the mouth , whether literal or figurative

verses.en: Don’t be hasty to go out of his presence. Don’t persist in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him,
verses.zh: 不要急躁离开王的面前，不要固执行恶，因为他凡事都随自己的心意而行。

words.g: to tremble inwardly , i.e.  be   alarmed or agitated

verses.en: for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
verses.zh: 王的话本有权力，谁敢问他说「你做甚么」呢？

verses.en: Whoever keeps the commandment shall not come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure.
verses.zh: 凡遵守命令的，必不经历祸患；智慧人的心能辨明时候和定理（原文是审判；下节同）。

words.g: a command, whether human or divine

verses.en: For there is a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him.
verses.zh: 各样事务成就都有时候和定理，因为人的苦难重压在他身上。

verses.en: For he doesn’t know that which will be; for who can tell him how it will be?
verses.zh: 他不知道将来的事，因为将来如何，谁能告诉他呢？

verses.en: There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver those who practice it.
verses.zh: 无人有权力掌管生命，将生命留住；也无人有权力掌管死期；这场争战，无人能免；邪恶也不能救那好行邪恶的人。

words.g: to + to restrict, by act  or word
to be smooth, i.e.  to escape

verses.en: All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every work that is done under the sun. There is a time in which one man has power over another to his hurt.
verses.zh: 这一切我都见过，也专心查考日光之下所做的一切事。有时这人管辖那人，令人受害。

verses.en: So I saw the wicked buried. Indeed they came also from holiness. They went and were forgotten in the city where they did this. This also is vanity.
verses.zh: 我见恶人埋葬，归入坟墓；又见行正直事的离开圣地，在城中被人忘记。这也是虚空。

words.g: and + to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of

verses.en: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.zh: 因为断定罪名不立刻施刑，所以世人满心作恶。

verses.en: Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.
verses.zh: 罪人虽然作恶百次，倒享长久的年日；然而我准知道，敬畏神的，就是在他面前敬畏的人，终久必得福乐。

verses.en: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow, because he doesn’t fear God.
verses.zh: 恶人却不得福乐，也不得长久的年日；这年日好像影儿，因他不敬畏神。

verses.en: There is a vanity which is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
verses.zh: 世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人所遭遇的，反照恶人所行的；又有恶人所遭遇的，反照义人所行的。我说，这也是虚空。

verses.en: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
verses.zh: 我就称赞快乐，原来人在日光之下，莫强如吃喝快乐；因为他在日光之下，神赐他一生的年日，要从劳碌中，时常享受所得的。

words.g: and + to address in aloud tone, i.e.  loud
used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (even though eyes see no sleep day or night),
verses.zh: 我专心求智慧，要看世上所做的事。（有昼夜不睡觉不合眼的。）

words.g: the + ado, i.e.  employment or  an affair

verses.en: then I saw all the work of God, that man can’t find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he won’t find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won’t be able to find it.
verses.zh: 我就看明神一切的作为，知道人查不出日光之下所做的事；任凭他费多少力寻查，都查不出来，就是智慧人虽想知道，也是查不出来。

words.g: in + which, that + because of, which
used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it is love or hatred, man doesn’t know it; all is before them.
verses.zh: 我将这一切事放在心上，详细考究，就知道义人和智慧人，并他们的作为都在神手中；或是爱，或是恨，都在他们的前面，人不能知道。

words.g: and + to + to bore, i.e.  examine

verses.en: All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him who sacrifices, and to him who doesn’t sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; he who takes an oath, as he who fears an oath.
verses.zh: 凡临到众人的事都是一样：义人和恶人都遭遇一样的事；好人，洁净人和不洁净人，献祭的与不献祭的，也是一样。好人如何，罪人也如何；起誓的如何，怕起誓的也如何。

words.g: something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune
and + to + foul in a religious sense
the + to seven oneself, i.e. swear

verses.en: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all. Yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
verses.zh: 在日光之下所行的一切事上有一件祸患，就是众人所遭遇的都是一样，并且世人的心充满了恶；活着的时候心里狂妄，后来就归死人那里去了。

words.g: something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune

verses.en: For to him who is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.zh: 与一切活人相连的，那人还有指望，因为活着的狗比死了的狮子更强。

verses.en: For the living know that they will die, but the dead don’t know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten.
verses.zh: 活着的人知道必死；死了的人毫无所知，也不再得赏赐；他们的名无人记念。

words.g: to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of

verses.en: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy has perished long ago; neither do they any longer have a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
verses.zh: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，早都消灭了。在日光之下所行的一切事上，他们永不再有分了。

words.g: extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works.
verses.zh: 你只管去欢欢喜喜吃你的饭，心中快乐喝你的酒，因为神已经悦纳你的作为。

words.g: extent of time, i.e. a great while

verses.en: Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil.
verses.zh: 你的衣服当时常洁白，你头上也不要缺少膏油。

verses.en: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity, for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun.
verses.zh: 在你一生虚空的年日，就是神赐你在日光之下虚空的年日，当同你所爱的妻，快活度日，因为那是你生前在日光之下劳碌的事上所得的分。

words.g: and + in + toil, i.e. wearing effort + +you/your
thou and thee, or  ye and you

verses.en: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
verses.zh: 凡你手所当做的事要尽力去做；因为在你所必去的阴间没有工作，没有谋算，没有知识，也没有智慧。

words.g: thou and thee, or  ye and you

verses.en: I returned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
verses.zh: 我又转念：见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢；力战的未必得胜；智慧的未必得粮食；明哲的未必得资财；灵巧的未必得喜悦。所临到众人的是在乎当时的机会。

words.g: to + to separate mentally , i.e. understand

verses.en: For man also doesn’t know his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them.
verses.zh: 原来人也不知道自己的定期。鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，祸患忽然临到的时候，世人陷在其中也是如此。

verses.en: I have also seen wisdom under the sun in this way, and it seemed great to me.
verses.zh: 我见日光之下有一样智慧，据我看乃是广大，

verses.en: There was a little city, and few men within it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
verses.zh: 就是有一小城，其中的人数稀少，有大君王来攻击，修筑营垒，将城围困。

verses.en: Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.zh: 城中有一个贫穷的智慧人，他用智慧救了那城，却没有人记念那穷人。

words.g: and + to be smooth, i.e.  to escape

verses.en: Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.zh: 我就说，智慧胜过勇力；然而那贫穷人的智慧被人藐视，他的话也无人听从。

verses.en: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
verses.zh: 宁可在安静之中听智慧人的言语，不听掌管愚昧人的喊声。

words.g: in + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.zh: 智慧胜过打仗的兵器；但一个罪人能败坏许多善事。

verses.en: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
verses.zh: 死苍蝇使做香的膏油发出臭气；这样，一点愚昧也能败坏智慧和尊荣。

words.g: from + weight, but only figuratively in a good sense

verses.en: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.zh: 智慧人的心居右；愚昧人的心居左。

verses.en: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
verses.zh: 并且愚昧人行路显出无知，对众人说，他是愚昧人。

verses.en: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
verses.zh: 掌权者的心若向你发怒，不要离开你的本位，因为柔和能免大过。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
verses.zh: 我见日光之下有一件祸患，似乎出于掌权的错误，

words.g: like + a mistake or inadvertent transgression

verses.en: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
verses.zh: 就是愚昧人立在高位；富足人坐在低位。

words.g: and + rich, whether literal or figurative

verses.en: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
verses.zh: 我见过仆人骑马，王子像仆人在地上步行。

verses.en: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
verses.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中；拆墙垣的，必为蛇所咬。

verses.en: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.
verses.zh: 凿开（或译：挪移）石头的，必受损伤；劈开木头的，必遭危险。

words.g: to pull up, especially the tent-pins
to carve, i.e. fabricate or fashion

verses.en: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
verses.zh: 铁器钝了，若不将刃磨快，就必多费气力；但得智慧指教，便有益处。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
and + probably a force, whether of men

verses.en: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
verses.zh: 未行法术以先，蛇若咬人，后行法术也是无益。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
verses.zh: 智慧人的口说出恩言；愚昧人的嘴吞灭自己。

words.g: the mouth , whether literal or figurative

verses.en: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.zh: 他口中的言语起头是愚昧；他话的末尾是奸恶的狂妄。

words.g: the mouth , whether literal or figurative + +him/his/it
and + the last or end, hence
the mouth , whether literal or figurative + +him/his/it

verses.en: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
verses.zh: 愚昧人多有言语，人却不知将来有甚么事；他身后的事谁能告诉他呢？

verses.en: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
verses.zh: 凡愚昧人，他的劳碌使自己困乏，因为连进城的路，他也不知道。

words.g: the + fat, i.e.  stupid or silly

verses.en: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
verses.zh: 邦国啊，你的王若是孩童，你的群臣早晨宴乐，你就有祸了！

words.g: a boy , from the age of infancy to adolescence

verses.en: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.zh: 邦国啊，你的王若是贵胄之子，你的群臣按时吃喝，为要补力，不为酒醉，你就有福了！

verses.en: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
verses.zh: 因人懒惰，房顶塌下；因人手懒，房屋滴漏。

words.g: the + something meeting, i.e. a frame

verses.en: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
verses.zh: 设摆筵席是为喜笑。酒能使人快活；钱能叫万事应心。

verses.en: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
verses.zh: 你不可咒诅君王，也不可心怀此念；在你卧房也不可咒诅富户。因为空中的鸟必传扬这声音，有翅膀的也必述说这事。

verses.en: Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.
verses.zh: 当将你的粮食撒在水面，因为日久必能得着。

verses.en: Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight; for you don’t know what evil will be on the earth.
verses.zh: 你要分给七人，或分给八人，因为你不知道将来有甚么灾祸临到地上。

verses.en: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be.
verses.zh: 云若满了雨，就必倾倒在地上。树若向南倒，或向北倒，树倒在何处，就存在何处。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
verses.zh: 看风的，必不撒种；望云的，必不收割。

verses.en: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
verses.zh: 风从何道来，骨头在怀孕妇人的胎中如何长成，你尚且不得知道；这样，行万事之神的作为，你更不得知道。

words.g: just so, referring to the previous or following context

verses.en: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
verses.zh: 早晨要撒你的种，晚上也不要歇你的手，因为你不知道哪一样发旺；或是早撒的，或是晚撒的，或是两样都好。

words.g: and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!

verses.en: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.zh: 光本是佳美的，眼见日光也是可悦的。

verses.en: Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
verses.zh: 人活多年，就当快乐多年；然而也当想到黑暗的日子。因为这日子必多，所要来的都是虚空。

words.g: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
to live, whether literally or figuratively
which, that + to come, go in

verses.en: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.zh: 少年人哪，你在幼年时当快乐。在幼年的日子，使你的心欢畅，行你心所愿行的，看你眼所爱看的；却要知道，为这一切的事，神必审问你。

verses.en: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
verses.zh: 所以，你当从心中除掉愁烦，从肉体克去邪恶；因为一生的开端和幼年之时，都是虚空的。

words.g: and + the + a dawning, i.e.  juvenescence

verses.en: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them;”
verses.zh: 你趁着年幼、衰败的日子尚未来到，就是你所说，我毫无喜乐的那些年日未曾临近之先，当记念造你的主。

verses.en: Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.zh: 不要等到日头、光明、月亮、星宿变为黑暗，雨后云彩反回，

verses.en: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
verses.zh: 看守房屋的发颤，有力的屈身，推磨的稀少就止息，从窗户往外看的都昏暗；

words.g: which, that + to shake off, i.e.  to agitate
the + probably a force, whether of men

verses.en: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
verses.zh: 街门关闭，推磨的响声微小，雀鸟一叫，人就起来，唱歌的女子也都衰微。

words.g: something swinging, i.e. the valve of adoor

verses.en: yes, they shall be afraid of heights, and terrors will be on the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets;
verses.zh: 人怕高处，路上有惊慌，杏树开花，蚱蜢成为重担，人所愿的也都废掉；因为人归他永远的家，吊丧的在街上往来。

words.g: and + to carry , or  be burdensome
and + to break up , i.e. to violate
the + to tear the hair and beat the breasts

verses.en: before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
verses.zh: 银链折断，金罐破裂，瓶子在泉旁损坏，水轮在井口破烂，

words.g: a rope , especially a measuring line
and + to crack in pieces, literally or figuratively
and + to crack in pieces, literally or figuratively

verses.en: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.zh: 尘土仍归于地，灵仍归于赐灵的神。

words.g: like + which, that + to be, become

verses.en: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “All is vanity!”
verses.zh: 传道者说：「虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。」

verses.en: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.zh: 再者，传道者因有智慧，仍将知识教训众人；又默想，又考查，又陈说许多箴言。

words.g: a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature

verses.en: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
verses.zh: 传道者专心寻求可喜悦的言语，是凭正直写的诚实话。

verses.en: The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.zh: 智慧人的言语好像刺棍；会中之师的言语又像钉稳的钉子，都是一个牧者所赐的。

verses.en: Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.zh: 我儿，还有一层，你当受劝戒：着书多，没有穷尽；读书多，身体疲倦。

verses.en: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.zh: 这些事都已听见了，总意就是：敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，这是人所当尽的本分（或译：这是众人的本分）。

words.g: a command, whether human or divine + +him/his/it

verses.en: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
verses.zh: 因为人所做的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。

words.g: to veil from sight, i.e. conceal
used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
and + used very widely as demonstrative, lo!
